title: IRS disputes and accountant liability — three clients
instructions: Answer each question about Kendall's IRS dispute and about lawsuits against Kendall's audit firm, Ashby & Lowe CPAs.

exhibits.title: Kendall's IRS matter
exhibits.content:
- Kendall's Year 1 return was filed April 10, Year 2 (due April 15, Year 2).
- The IRS examined the return and issued a statutory notice of deficiency on March 1, Year 5.
- Kendall doesn't want to pay the tax before contesting it.

exhibits.title: Lawsuits against Ashby & Lowe
exhibits.content:
- **First National** loaned money to an audit client; Ashby & Lowe knew the statements were for First National's loan decision.
- **Harbor Credit** also lent to the client; Ashby & Lowe knew the client would show the statements to "a few banks" but didn't know which ones.
- **An investor** bought the client's newly registered shares and claims the registration statement's audited statements were materially misstated.

rows.label: Last day the IRS could normally assess Year 1 tax (no fraud, no large omission)
rows.explanation: An early return is treated as filed on the due date; the period is 3 years.

rows.label: The forum Kendall should use
rows.explanation: The only forum that doesn't require payment first.

parts.prompt: Can each plaintiff sue Ashby & Lowe for ordinary negligence under the stated rule?

rows.label: First National — Ultramares state
rows.explanation: A known user and known purpose (near privity).

rows.label: Harbor Credit — Ultramares state
rows.explanation: Not specifically known to the auditor.

rows.label: Harbor Credit — Restatement §552 state
rows.explanation: A member of a limited, known class of users.

parts.prompt: The investor's claim under §11 of the 1933 Act

rows.label: Must the investor prove Ashby & Lowe was negligent?
options: No — the burden shifts to the auditor to show due diligence
rows.answer: No — the burden shifts to the auditor to show due diligence
rows.explanation: §11 imposes liability unless the auditor proves a defense.

rows.label: Ashby & Lowe's best defense
options: The investor didn't read the auditor's report
rows.explanation: A reasonable investigation and reasonable belief the statements were true.
